## What's new

- **Liquid Glass on macOS** — the main window and the recording prompt now use macOS's native glass material (on macOS 26 and later), following the app's light/dark theme. On older macOS, Windows, and Linux, the prompt keeps its previous look.
- **Microsoft Store (MSIX) package for Windows** — TypeAloud can now be distributed through the Microsoft Store. When installed from the Store, the app detects this and leaves updates to the Store instead of its own updater.
- **Smarter correction of near-miss spellings** — words you add to your dictionary (and a built-in list of common tech terms) are now used to fix heard text that's slightly off — e.g. a name coming out as "Nematron" one time and "namatron" another is corrected to match. This also helps with local (offline) transcription, which previously had no way to be nudged toward the right spelling.

## Improvements

- The app is now **TypeAloud** everywhere — window titles, permission prompts, the tray tooltip, and installers. On first launch after updating, your settings, history, and downloaded models move over automatically, and launch-at-login keeps working.
- TypeAloud is now open source under the GPL-3.0 license.

## Fixes

- Spelled-out letters like "c p p" now merge into "cpp" regardless of letter case; previously only the fully capitalized form ("C P P") merged correctly.
- Fixed a bug where, in rare cases, upgrading could leave settings, history, or a downloaded model behind instead of carrying them over to the new app data location.

## What's new
- Dictionary now supports automatic replacement rules: type what SayType mis-hears and what it should say instead, and every rule rewrites the final text for every transcription engine (cloud and local). Rules are entered through a simple two-field form (add, replace, remove) instead of needing to learn any special syntax.
- Added built-in corrections for commonly misheard terms (e.g. Supabase, Wispr Flow, Parakeet, Hacker News, Vercel, Walter Isaacson, "Claude Code").
- Update checks and downloads (both the app updater and local speech-model/runtime downloads) now also try a mirror hosted in mainland China, chosen automatically based on your time zone, to help users there who can't reach GitHub well.
- Added optional, anonymous daily usage statistics (dictation counts, failures, characters inserted, engine used) to help guide development. It's on by default but can be turned off at any time from Settings or during onboarding; turning it off deletes the locally stored data.

## Improvements
- Shortened the wait after you release the hotkey: SayType now cuts long dictations into chunks earlier (starting at a 20-second pause instead of 55 seconds), so the final piece of audio to transcribe is much shorter. Median post-release wait dropped noticeably in testing.
- Pause detection for chunking is now based on actual elapsed time rather than raw audio capture blocks, making cut points more reliable on Windows and Linux where tiny internal pauses (e.g. inside a word) could previously be mistaken for a sentence break.

## Fixes
- Fixed a bug where a brief stretch of near-silence at the end of a cut dictation could be transcribed as a stray, often nonsensical word or phrase (e.g. "嗯。" or "no.", even in the wrong language). That trailing silence is now detected and skipped instead of being sent to the transcription engine.

The waveform shrinks first, then the hint text wraps onto up to two lines, breaking only at natural word/punctuation boundaries so shortcut labels like "Ctrl + Shift" stay together.

## What's new
- **Tap-to-recover, double-tap-to-lock hotkey**: A quick, short press of Ctrl+Shift (under 500 ms, with no second press) is now a "tap." If a failed-dictation card is showing, tapping re-inserts that card's text at your cursor instead of discarding it — no need to reopen History and copy/paste. Without a card showing, a tap behaves as before (a mis-trigger cancel). A second quick press within 350 ms instead **locks** the recording hands-free: it keeps recording without holding the keys down, until you press again, hit Escape, or 12 minutes pass. A tap followed by holding the keys is treated as a normal dictation, and long-hold recordings show a short tip about the double-tap feature (shown at most three times).
  - Note for Windows users: switching keyboard layouts with Ctrl+Shift twice in quick succession can accidentally trigger a lock.
- **Filler-word removal**: Final transcriptions can now automatically drop hesitation fillers (嗯, 呃, and standalone 额) along with the surrounding pause punctuation, e.g. "觉得，呃，我们" becomes "觉得，我们". Fillers that are quoted, listed alongside other interjections, named, used as parts of words, or reported as someone's spoken answer are left untouched. A new "Remove filler words" setting controls this and is **on by default**; results that were only filler become empty and are treated as no speech.

## Fixes
- Filler removal no longer strips 嗯/呃 when they appear inside quotation marks (“”, ‘’, 「」, 『』, or straight double quotes), since quoted speech should stay verbatim (e.g. 他说："嗯，好吧。" keeps its 嗯). Unmatched quote marks (like an apostrophe, or a dropped closing quote) are not treated as quoting.
